name: Ohad
overview: Ohad was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, known primarily as a son of Simeon. He is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking his place in the early patriarchal history of Israel as recorded in Genesis. His identity is closely tied to his tribal affiliation and family lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Ohad appears only once in Scripture and no specific meaning or divine origin is provided for it. It is simply recorded as a proper name without additional significance noted in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ohad as a son of Simeon, establishing his direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Ohad's significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, a foundational event in the biblical narrative that sets the stage for the later deliverance of Israel. As a son of Simeon, Ohad represents one branch of the twelve tribes, contributing to the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham regarding his descendants. His mention underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant through the generations.
